    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

     

    Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.

     

    You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.

     

    We are a distributed team that values curiosity, sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous learning. We teach and learn from one another, adapt as the threat landscape changes, and focus our effort according to business needs and risk.

    ","id":"cb29d857-395b-401d-9749-367e666ff870","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Identify detection opportunities, define clear telemetry requirements, and partner with the detection infrastructure squad and data owners to make the signals needed for detection and investigation available.

    • Develop, test, tune, and maintain detections across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, email, and other security-relevant environments.

    • Investigate and prioritize alerts, determine their security impact, and participate in incident containment and remediation.

    • Build repeatable investigation workflows and playbooks for alert triage, evidence collection, decision-making, escalation, containment, and response.

    • Improve proactive threat-identification and threat-hunting capabilities using internal telemetry and external threat intelligence.

    • Create cutting-edge AI workflows for Detection and Response that enrich alerts, gather and analyze evidence, guide investigations, and automate repetitive response work while preserving appropriate human judgment and oversight.

    • Measure detection effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and tune detections to balance security value, fidelity, and analyst workload.

    • Use SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and related security platforms to research threats, develop detections, investigate alerts, and validate security outcomes.

    • Share knowledge, document decisions, and communicate security findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in an ambiguous and rapidly changing environment.

    • You have 3+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, detection engineering, or closely related work.

    • You understand how analysts triage and investigate alerts and how detection quality affects their decisions and workload.

    • You know how to create and tune detections based on attacker behavior, available telemetry, and an expected investigation path.

    • You are experienced with security platforms such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or comparable monitoring and response technologies.

    • You can write code or use an automation platform to analyze security telemetry, enrich alerts, build investigation workflows, and remove repetitive work. Experience with Python or a similar language is valuable.

    • You understand modern detection-as-code practices, including GitHub, peer review, CI/CD, testing, and safely managing production detection content.

    • You have experience working with at least one major cloud platform, such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure.

    • You understand common threats affecting SaaS-oriented corporate and production environments.

    • You care about clear documentation, inclusive collaboration, and explaining security concepts to people with different backgrounds and levels of expertise.

    • You are excited to create and critically evaluate cutting-edge AI workflows for detection development, alert triage, security investigations, and response, while applying sound security judgment and appropriate human oversight.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Security engineers at Spotify help protect our environment and more than 700 million users. Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

    As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

     

    ","id":"1ee5dcb7-a5fe-465b-91da-d42ebab374c8","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Build and improve agentic AI workflows that turn security vulnerability findings into tested, review-ready code changes for engineering teams across Spotify.

    • Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the quality of automated fixes, including correctness, completeness, safety, build and test success, and pull request merge rates.

    • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.

    • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

    • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

    • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

    • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have experience in software engineering, particularly within security engineering, developer experience, or internal infrastructure.

    • You can confidently read, understand, and write code in one or more languages such as Java, Python, Scala, C++, or TypeScript.

    • You have experience designing and building scalable systems, with an understanding of software architecture and reliable engineering practices.

    • You have worked with agentic AI systems or AI-assisted development workflows and understand how to apply them to real-world engineering challenges.

    • You understand common security risks, attack vectors, and vulnerabilities, including those affecting AI and machine learning systems, and approaches to mitigating them.

    • You have experience integrating security tools or automated workflows into production engineering environments.

    • You are familiar with agentic AI frameworks and approaches to evaluating the quality, reliability, and safety of AI-generated outputs.

    • You enjoy collaborating across teams, learning from feedback, and navigating ambiguity. You're comfortable experimenting with new approaches while balancing innovation with thoughtful security decisions.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

    We own music content ingestion at Spotify, which is how music from labels, distributors and other partners gets onto the platform. We receive industry-standard deliveries, validate them, and turn them into the catalog data that teams across Spotify build on, including lyrics, rights and supply data. As we add new content types and partners, we’re building an ingestion platform that scales without a custom build every time.

    We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 

    Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to build secure, reliable, and scalable authentication experiences that have a direct impact on millions of people every day.

    ","id":"813b4b62-429c-42e9-a8f7-59e9412fb287","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do ","content":"
  • Collaborate with a highly autonomous and supportive engineering squad responsible for Spotify’s delegated authorization and session management platforms.
  • Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS.
  • Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms.
  • Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation.
  • Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance.
  • Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences.
  • Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have strong proficiency in C++, along with experience building native iOS applications in Swift, or you're excited to develop your expertise in Swift while applying your C++ skills.
  • You have experience designing, building, or maintaining security-sensitive systems such as authorization, authentication, token management, credential storage, or related platforms.

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.

    Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.

    Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    ","id":"babebec3-0061-4c39-a4ad-c51a54d23567","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
  • Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
  • Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
  • Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
  • Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
  • Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
  • You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
  • You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
  • You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
  • You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
  • You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
  • You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
  • You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.

    We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.

    You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale.     ","id":"9d1c90b5-a8a4-4218-b2f3-7bbaefae7fd1","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation.
  • Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions.
  • Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles.
  • Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences.
  • Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify.
  • Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms.
  • Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging.
  • Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data.
  • Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change.
  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats.
  • You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions.
  • You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time.
  • You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content.
  • You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate.
  • You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent.
  • You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences.
  • You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes.
  • You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners.
  • You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience.
  • You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI.
  • You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    Growlithe is a fast-moving squad within Spotify's Conversation Product Area, focused on bringing emerging Search and agentic experiences to life. We explore, define, build, validate, and optimize new ideas to help listeners discover the content they love. Our work spans personalized Search, music video discovery and ranking, audiobook Search expansion, and the foundations of more social Search experiences.

    We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to help shape the next generation of Search at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, personalization, and product development, turning complex challenges into intuitive discovery experiences for millions of listeners.

    As a Senior Product Quality Analyst, you’ll bring a dedicated evaluation perspective to the team.     Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

  • Create intuitive internal products that enable business teams to launch, configure, and manage Premium offers through secure, guided workflows.

  • Develop GraphQL and gRPC APIs that connect frontend applications with distributed platform services.

  • Design efficient database schemas, implement data migrations, and optimize application performance using PostgreSQL.

  • Build secure, reliable, and auditable systems that support business-critical financial operations and SOX-compliant approval workflows.

  • Collaborate with engineers across the Subscriptions Mission to evolve shared platform capabilities, improve developer experience, and increase platform reliability.

  • Write maintainable, well-tested code while contributing to technical design, architecture discussions, code reviews, and continuous improvement.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to help maintain the reliability and availability of services powering Spotify Premium.

  • You have hands-on experience with PostgreSQL or another relational database, including schema design, migrations, and query optimization.

  • Define the technical direction for policy enforcement infrastructure 

  • Architect enforcement capabilities as a shared platform designed to be consumed by multiple product teams rather

  • Design and evolve multi-signal orchestration systems that enable configurable, auditable policy enforcement at scale across content types and product surfaces

  • Build the data foundation that makes enforcement decisions durable and reusable

  • Own the hardest API and contract decisions: schema design, versioning strategy, and how enforcement interfaces evolve without breaking the teams that depend on them

  • Establish integration standards for teams onboarding onto shared enforcement infrastructure, and work directly with consuming teams to execute migrations with clean cutoffs and clear end states

  • Influence architecture across detection, signal processing, and enforcement workflows so that the underlying primitives stay coherent as the platform scales

  • Mentor engineers and set the bar for how the team reasons about API design, data modeling, and the downstream compliance consequences of infrastructure choices

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world.

    As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences that delight users and drive meaningful impact. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking models from research to production, driving technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solving complex personalization challenges at global scale.

    ","id":"281e7db9-86ba-4a1c-8773-c23b96ed32dc","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience.

    • Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally.

    • Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences.

    • Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.

    • Partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and designers to define and execute experimentation strategies.

    • Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency.

    • Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale.

    • Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of personalization systems.

    • Mentor and support other machine learning engineers, helping raise the bar across the team.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 8+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments.

    • You have deep expertise in recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms.

    • You have strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch.

    • You are experienced with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques including SFT, distillation, and LoRA.

    • You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization.

    • You care deeply about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful application of machine learning.

    • You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, and you influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team

    • You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes.

    • You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks.

    • You are experienced building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location.

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.


    Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world.


    As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences that delight users and drive meaningful impact. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking models from research to production, driving technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solving complex personalization challenges at global scale.

    ","id":"9761af44-be41-43ca-8c01-79cdbb2aef93","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience.

    • Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally.

    • Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences.

    • Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.

    • Partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and designers to define and execute experimentation strategies.

    • Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency.

    • Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale.

    • Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of personalization systems.

    • Mentor and support other machine learning engineers, helping raise the bar across the team.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 8+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments.

    • You have deep expertise in recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms.

    • You have strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch.

    • You are experienced with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques including SFT, distillation, and LoRA.

    • You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization.

    • You care deeply about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful application of machine learning.

    • You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, and you influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team

    • You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes.

    • You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks.

    • You are experienced building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms.

    In your role, you will focus on compliance and reporting. Spotify reports indirect taxes in more than 90 countries globally and you will be a key member of the team responsible for ensuring the completeness, timeliness and accuracy of Spotify’s global indirect tax compliance obligations. You will work in close collaboration with global tax team members in both Stockholm and New York, and work cross functionally with various accounting and finance teams.

    We are a team of highly skilled and dedicated colleagues and we offer a challenging and dynamic role in an ever changing environment with the opportunity to take on much responsibility in a rapidly growing international company. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences audio.

    ","id":"d2489df3-87cb-48bb-81af-83aab5f03bdc","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Prepare indirect tax returns ensuring they are filed timely and accurate.
  • Calculate indirect taxes and ensure timely payments.
  • Analyze data and transactions to ensure correct reporting.
  • Assist with gathering and analyzing data for indirect tax audits and internal audits.
  • Support in monitoring Indirect Tax rules and regulations all over the world.
  • Coordinate with, and support, Finance and Accounting teams as necessary and assist in processes that involve indirect tax.
  • Assist with new tax registrations where needed.
  • Work with external service providers and foreign tax authorities.
  • Participate in process improvement projects
  • Assist in other tax compliance areas such as digital services tax.
  • Other projects as required.

  • University degree with relevant education such as law degree, accounting, CPA, or any combination thereof.
  • Approximately 2 years of relevant tax related work experience.
  • Experience from indirect tax compliance work on a global scale is a big plus.
  • Excellent English skills, both verbally and written. Other language skills are helpful.
  • Experience with financial systems (we use NetSuite): ERPs, consolidation tools and management reporting tools.
  • Strong skills in the Google suite and/or Microsoft Office including the ability to prepare robust models and the ability and desire to learn new software platforms.
  • Strong attention to detail, ability to drive work and assist with process improvements.
  • Self-starter, capable of working independently with strong initiative and flexibility.

Tech.eu https://tech.eu en Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:23:24 +0000 hourly 1 <![CDATA[Startups respond to Britain's budget, Greentech Alliance acquires Intermobility, and Europe’s biggest seed rounds of Q3]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/#comments This week, we tracked more than 60 tech funding deals worth over €1.3 billion and over 10 exits, M&A transactions, rumours, and related news stories across Europe.

Britain has no shortage of startup ambition, but can it turn that success into companies that scale and stay? This week's UK Budget introduced Founders' Relief and a raft of measures supporting entrepreneurs, including expanded employee share options, initiatives for female founders and further investment in AI. It's a welcome signal, but tax incentives alone won't solve Britain's scaleup problem.

The UK attracted €14 billion in startup funding in H1 2026, yet access to later-stage capital, customers, talent and infrastructure remains a challenge.

In my follow-up feature, I spoke to founders and ecosystem leaders about what needs to change, from closing regional and gender funding gaps to helping companies commercialise and compete globally. The real test isn't how many startups Britain creates, but how many it can help grow into lasting global businesses.

Want to stay in the know? If email is more your thing, you can always subscribe to our newsletter and receive a more robust version of this round-up delivered to your inbox.

❗ Want to explore the data in more detail? The free, open-access Tech.eu Funding Explorer offers deeper insights into funding rounds, investor activity, company profiles and market trends.

Either way, let's get you up to speed.

Diagnostics, AI and patient monitoring

Earlier diagnosis, more accurate assessments and continuous patient monitoring are critical against ageing populations, growing demand and shortages of medical professionals. Checkpoint Care (Bulgaria) 

Check Point Care develops remote patient monitoring tech. Its platform combines wearable medical devices, continuous physiological monitoring and AI-powered clinical decision support. It aims to reduce preventable deaths, hospital readmissions and pressure on healthcare systems by enabling earlier detection and intervention.

The company's wearable devices continuously collect clinical-grade data, including ECG, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and body temperature.  This information is transmitted to a centralised digital platform, where AI algorithms analyse physiological patterns and generate digital biomarkers.

Ligence (Lithuania)

Ligence develops AI-powered software that automates the analysis of cardiac ultrasound images, helping cardiologists assess heart function and identify potential abnormalities. Its flagship product, Ligence Heart, uses machine learning to analyse echocardiograms, automatically identify anatomical structures, perform measurements and generate structured reports. 

The company says its technology can reduce routine examination and reporting workflows from approximately 30 minutes to 15 minutes, potentially allowing hospitals to assess more patients without proportionally increasing staffing requirements.

The technology is designed to integrate with existing hospital imaging systems, reducing the manual work involved in cardiac diagnostics. Ligence has achieved European CE marking and two US FDA 510(k) clearances, the second granted in April 2026 for an updated version of Ligence Heart featuring automated left ventricular strain analysis.

MiMARK Diagnostics is developing molecular diagnostic technologies to improve the detection of gynaecological diseases, particularly endometrial cancer.  The company is focused on identifying disease-associated biomarkers in gynaecological samples to provide more accurate, less invasive diagnostic methods that can be incorporated into routine clinical practice.

Endometrial cancer is one of the most common gynaecological cancers, yet diagnosis can involve invasive procedures, including endometrial biopsies and hysteroscopy. More accessible testing could reduce unnecessary invasive procedures while supporting earlier identification of disease.

Medical devices and interventional technologies

Medical device innovation is transforming how clinicians treat serious conditions, particularly where conventional interventions are invasive, carry significant risks or have limited effectiveness. 

Anaconda Biomed ( Spain)

Barcelona-based Anaconda Biomed develops medical devices to treat acute ischaemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery supplying the brain. Its technology focuses on mechanical thrombectomy, a minimally invasive procedure in which physicians use catheters to remove clots and restore blood flow.

The company's ANA Funnel Catheter features a self-expanding, funnel-shaped design intended to improve clot capture, restrict blood flow during retrieval and reduce the risk of clot fragments travelling into smaller vessels. Speed and effectiveness are critical in stroke treatment, as delays in restoring blood flow can result in permanent neurological damage, disability or death. 

Anaconda's tech works alongside existing thrombectomy devices, potentially improving the efficiency of clot removal and reducing complications. Its development reflects the growing importance of specialised neurovascular technologies that can improve outcomes in time-critical medical emergencies.

In September 2026, Anaconda Biomed secured $56 million in financing.

CorWave (France)

CorWave is developing implantable heart pumps for patients with advanced heart failure, using technology inspired by the movement of marine animals.  The technology is designed to reproduce more natural, pulsatile blood flow, adapting to the patient's 

Its Left Ventricular Assist System (LVAS) uses a patented wave membrane to propel blood through the device, rather than the rotary mechanisms used in conventional heart pumps. Existing ventricular assist devices can sustain patients for years, but risks such as bleeding, stroke and blood clot formation remain significant concerns.

CorWave aims to address these limitations by preserving the natural pulse and improving the interaction between mechanical circulatory support and the cardiovascular system. 

In May 2025 CoreWave’s LVAS was implanted in a patient for the first time at St Vincent's Hospital in Sydney, Australia. The patient successfully underwent a heart transplant after 84 days of mechanical support, with no device-related serious adverse events recorded at 30 days. 

Biotechnology and advanced therapeutics

Advances by European biotech companies in genomics, precision medicine, immunotherapy and cellular reprogramming are creating opportunities to target the underlying biological mechanisms of disease rather than simply managing symptoms. 

Arctic Therapeutics (Iceland)

Arctic Therapeutics is developing treatments for complex neurological and inflammatory diseases, drawing on genetic research and population-level health data to identify potential therapeutic targets. 

Its approach combines insights from human genetics with drug development to investigate disease mechanisms and identify opportunities for more targeted treatments.

By using genetic insights to understand the biological drivers of disease, Arctic Therapeutics aims to develop treatments that address underlying mechanisms rather than symptoms alone.

The company focuses on rare neurological diseases and forms of dementia. 

In 2025, Arctic Therapeutics raised €26.5 million Series A.

Asgard Therapeutics (Sweden)

Asgard Therapeutics is developing a new approach to cancer immunotherapy based on in vivo cellular reprogramming. 

Rather than relying solely on conventional treatments that directly attack tumours, the company is investigating how to reprogram cancer cells to stimulate the body's immune system, potentially enabling it to recognise and target malignant cells. Its technology aims to convert tumour cells into cells with antigen-presenting properties, allowing them to activate immune responses against cancer.

This approach could potentially address some of the limitations of existing immunotherapies, which do not work for every patient or cancer type.

Christoph Rieche is a careful, measured speaker, so when he says “I will never forget it”, one tends to lock in.

Rewind to 2010ish, and Rieche, then a well-paid thirtysomething Goldman Sachs executive with itchy feet to launch a startup, met with Index Ventures co-founder Neil Rimer.

Rieche says: “Index was at the time already a pretty famous fund. I was in Geneva for business. Neil happened to be based there. I told him 'I can tell you about my world. Why don’t you tell me more about the VC world?' We were sitting in this meeting, and he said 'we just did an investment, but we haven’t announced it yet. It’s in a company called Funding Circle, and they provide lending to small businesses.’”

The revelation appears to have kick-started Rieche, who had been mulling launching his own Funding Circle AKA Iwoca, into action, as soon after Iwoca was born.

Turning the clock back

Tech.eu is sat opposite Rieche, who is German, in Iwoca’s newish, fresh-smelling London offices (all creams, soft furnishings, and overhanging plants), as the 46-year-old winds back the clock to Iwoca’s early days. Back then, he says, fintech wasn’t a thing; Revolut and Monzo weren’t about and the brands of the day were Spotify and LoveFilm while Rieche was a habitué of Meetup.com (now part of Bending Spoons) where he met his co-founder.

Rieche has now been CEO at Iwoca for nearly 15 years, which, he admits, is a long stint steering a startup or scaleup. But could it all be coming to an end?

Iwoca up for sale?

Sky News reported in June this year that Iwoca, which has raised around £70m in equity and is backed by Augmentum and Commerzbank’s CommerzVentures, was up for sale.

It had hired tech investment bank Qatalyst Partners to oversee the auction, with a sale value of over £1bn. 

Rieche says: “We have shareholders that have been with us for 15 years, some of them. Our last financing round was in 2019, so our youngest shareholder is seven years in. They are all VCs. These kinds of people naturally look for liquidity. It’s quite likely that we will find them some liquidity. But it doesn’t have any impact on our strategy.”

Does that mean an outright sale, IPO or secondary share sale? “I don’t know, these conversations happen literally all the time.”

Iwoca’s launch

You might not have heard of it, but Iwoca is one of the UK’s fastest-growing small business lenders, providing funding for tens of thousands of businesses every year.

It launched in 2012, when Rieche and his co-founder, James Dear, a former Deutsche Bank quant trader (who is stepping down this year), spied an opportunity in the ruins of the financial crisis, which saw banks retreat from SME lending.

Rieche says he was enticed by helping underserved SMEs, the overall market opportunity, and disrupting the legacy banks with tech and data. Today, Iwoca (whose name derives from its mission brief: instant working capital, so I-wo-ca), employs over 700 staff, with offices in London, Leeds, Berlin and Frankfurt.

Iwoca’s offering

Iwoca’s flagship product is SME loans, which range from £1,000 to £1,000,000 in the UK and up to €500,000 in Germany. Loan origination leapt from £952m to £1.5bn in 2025, driving up revenues by 56 per cent to £366m in 2025, Iwoca’s latest financial figures show.

Profits, meanwhile, nearly doubled from £59m to £113m in the period. Its jump in revenues comes amid incumbent banks retreating from SME financing, with challengers like Iwoca eating up market share.

Iwoca, which uses open banking to speed up loan applications, likes to trumpet the speed of its loan approval process, which is largely automated (its record is two minutes and three seconds from a standing start for an approval).

Starling deal

Iwoca also offers loans to Monzo, Starling and Tide customers and other businesses through partnership deals.

On its recently announced deal with Starling, Rieche said: “It’s been a long time in the making. I met Anne Boden about this more than 10 years go. I have been doing this for 15 years now. One thing I have learnt is that things take time. You can’t break through everything in a couple of days.”

One of the big trends in fintech in recent years has been the rise in stablecoin technology but Iwoca says it has no plans to leverage the tech in its lending offering.

Amid observers saying that Iwoca had too narrow an offering, it has recently expanded its product portfolio.

Flushed with “excess liquidity” and “more cognitive energy”, Iwoca has launched a credit score product, business credit card, and an M&A platform to help business buy and sell businesses.

Sanctioned shareholder

In Iwoca’s latest financial results, under the regulatory risk category, there is a reference to London-based VC Redline Capital, which is one of Iwoca’s longest-standing shareholder and owns around a 10 per cent stake in Iwoca. Redline was funded by Vladimir Yevtushenkov, a Russian oligarch, whose daughter Tatiana Evtushenkova has served as its CEO.

In 2023, Redline’s investment in Iwoca was placed under an asset freeze due to sanctions imposed by the UK government related to Yevtushenkov, the billionaire founder of Sistema, the Russian telecoms and media conglomerate

This caused “quite a big headache” for Iwoca, Rieche says. Evtushenkova, who stood down as director of Redline in 2023 according to filings, was removed from the UK sanctions list in 2025.

Rieche says: “These are the great experiences you go through when you are building your own company. Very fortunately for us, that person in the end was removed from the sanctions list last year, so we don’t have any sanctioned shareholders anymore. So, it’s a solved problem.”

Will Iwoca carry out future funding soon? Rieche says no, pointing to Iwoca being profitable.

Running a startup

German stereotypes aside, Rieche is initially a reserved interviewee and appears a methodical man (he did nine months “solid” startup and VC research and two work placements before launching Iwoca).

But once he gets going, he speaks fluidly about the ups and downs of his job (“there are times obviously when you are more motivated than others”), why he’s swerving conferences these days, and London losing its lustre as a fintech hub. Typically, Rieche works from 8.30am until around 8pm, with half his time on Iwoca’s UK business, the rest divided up between its German business and new initiatives.

Of late, he has pulled back on overseas work travel, as he has attending conferences.

He said: “There’s too much to do with the team. The ROI on these events, I think is reasonably low. I spend most of my time with the team and significantly less with the external world.”

Outside work, Rieche, who has two children, spends weekend driving his children around, as well as having an interest in London’s cultural scene.

London losing its appeal

On London as a fintech hub, he says, it has “probably got worse” since he started Iwoca, pointing to an increase in tax and pulling back of entrepreneurs’ incentives (the interview takes place the Autumn Budget).

He says: “Wherever I am looking, things got less flexible for businesses.”

That said, London will remain Iwoca’s headquarters and London “is still a phenomenal city and a magnet”.

The future 

Iwoca has hitherto served more than 100,000 SMEs with loans, but its big ambition is to serve one million.

Whether it will get there and remain independent remains to be seen.

What is apparent is that Rieche has retained an entrepreneurial mindset, albeit with a heavier workload in light of his co-founder exiting. Rieche says his role is “constantly changing” with “different challenges”.

He says: “Now we have started these new initiatives; it really does add a completely new chapter for us.”

Chancellor John Healey summed up the problem the government is trying to address:

Europe's funding leader still has a scaleup problem

Britain is hardly starved of venture capital by European standards. The UK remains Europe's biggest destination for startup funding, and Tech.eu's H1 report recorded €14 billion in UK startup equity funding across 423 rounds in H1 2026, up 117.5 per cent year-on-year.

But can British companies access enough patient, later-stage capital to remain independent and scale globally from the UK, rather than eventually looking to US investors, buyers or markets?

Sam Goodsell, Partner and Head of Technology Sector at Menzies LLP, sees the tax change as an incentive for entrepreneurs to keep building rather than accept an early exit, but argues that tax incentives alone will not solve Britain's scaleup problem.

Owen Ensor, co-founder and CEO of cultivated meat startup Meatly, made a similar distinction:

“The new Founders’ Relief is a welcome announcement and a positive signal that Britain wants to reward entrepreneurs who take risks and build successful companies.

But the bigger opportunity is making Britain the best place in the world not just to start a company, but to scale one.”

Female founders welcome support — but barriers remain

The new programme for female founders adds to existing efforts to tackle the gender gap in venture funding, including the government-backed Women Backing Women initiative, which reached a £130 million first close earlier this year.

Laura Ashforth, co-founder and CEO of Lateral, welcomed the Budget's support but argued that encouraging entrepreneurship requires looking beyond investment incentives.

“We desperately need more people to take on the enormous personal and financial risks required to build the businesses that will drive the UK's future growth.

Taking the startup push beyond London

The UK's funding strength also disguises a longstanding geographic imbalance. While 53 per cent of high-growth businesses are based outside London, they receive only 39 per cent of the funding. Oxfordshire's recently launched Equinox 2035 Strategy, for example, aims to create 20 billion-dollar companies, attract more than £1 billion in annual investment and generate 30,000 jobs by 2035. That sits within a broader regional investment push.

The 2026 Budget includes £1 billion over four years for Priority Innovation Clusters, while UKRI's £500 million Local Innovation Partnerships Fund is targeting clusters across the UK. The British Business Bank is also deploying dedicated regional funds, including the £150 million Northern Scaleup Fund, targeting high-growth companies and university spinouts across northern England.

By July 2026, the Bank's Nations and Regions funds had invested more than £465 million into 1,254 businesses, attracting another £417 million in private capital. Government-backed funds can help fill regional investment gaps, but their success should ultimately be measured by whether they attract enough sustained private investment to reduce the need for public intervention.

Beyond funding: helping British startups commercialise and scale

The Budget includes £25 million for a new Venture Doctorates scheme and £16 million in proof-of-concept funding to help turn university research into commercial businesses.

The British Business Bank will receive an additional £5 billion, taking its total capitalisation to £30.6 billion.

Beyond expanding investment in venture capital funds, the Bank plans to introduce a venture debt product, giving growing companies another financing option without requiring them to surrender equity. But access to capital is only part of the challenge. Startups also need customers.

Planned public procurement reforms include a new Innovation Marketplace, launching in spring 2027, to connect innovative businesses with public-sector buyers. As the UK Business Angels Association notes in its Budget analysis, reforms to the Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) and Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS) also leave some industry concerns unresolved, including calls to increase the age limit for eligible businesses.

AI puts industrial policy to the test

The government's focus on AI offers a test of whether its investment strategy can translate into industrial growth. The Budget includes an additional £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund and £80 million to expand early-stage AI procurement, alongside support for the Sovereign AI Unit, AI Security Institute and a new Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme.

Peter Griffiths, founder and Executive Chairman of Argyll Data Development, pointed to an even more fundamental constraint:

“The Government has finally recognised that Britain's AI ambitions depend on electricity as much as investment.”

He contends that without compute, power and domestic customers, Britain risks financing the early stages of AI companies whose eventual economic value is captured elsewhere. From starting companies to keeping them

The UK has already shown it can produce promising startups and attract substantial venture investment. The harder task is ensuring those companies can access the capital, infrastructure and customers they need to become global businesses without leaving Britain.

The real measure of these initiatives will not be how many programmes are launched or how much funding is announced, but how many companies build lasting businesses in the UK.

A growing body of evidence on UPF’s

UPFs are designed to tempt, backed by clever marketing and often on special offer. In November 2025, an international team of researchers published a series in The Lancet linking the growing share of UPFs in diets worldwide to the rise in chronic disease.

Brussels has taken notice. In July, the European Commission asked its scientific advisers how the EU should define ultra-processed food. Their advice is expected in March 2027.

The Commission has also approached FLTRD co-founder Anke Kuik for her expertise.

“The fact that UPFs are now on the European agenda is an important step,” says Kuik. “It shows this isn’t a passing trend, but a problem that calls for a structural response.”

How does the PureScore work?

The PureScore rates products on three components that together determine the score:

Ingredients: the type and amount of added sugars, fats, salt and additives. Refined ingredients stripped of their nutrients also lower the score.

Processing techniques: processes such as heating, hydrogenation and extrusion that alter the natural structure of food. The more intensive the processing, the lower the score.

Organic certification: organic products score higher because they contain fewer pesticide residues. This structure reflects the three main ways UPFs are thought to affect health: loss of nutrients, the addition of harmful substances and a higher risk of overconsumption.

The FLTRD app now covers more than 150,000 products from seven supermarkets, all of which have a PureScore. This independent, science-based score rates a product’s degree of processing based on its ingredients and processing techniques, so people can easily make healthier choices. 

In the Netherlands, more than 35,000 people already use the app on iPhone and Android.

The goal is for 100 million people to use the PureScore to guide their grocery shopping within five years.

“This investment allows us to bring in the people we need to accelerate.

A structural shift in the market

“The European debate on ultra-processed food signals a structural shift in the market. As the European Commission explores which policy frameworks are needed, transparency is becoming a commercial priority for the food sector.

Alongside 4impact, several angel investors from the FMCG industry have participated in the round. One of them is Jeroen Lubbers, who now invests in healthy food initiatives after many years in the sector.
